title: Private Deployments — cross-team alignment huddle 2026-05-22
content:
Attendees: Aisha (owner), Marco (SRE), Linnea (Product), Tomoko (Security), Ravi (Solutions Eng), plus notes from Kara (on-call)

Purpose: quick cross-team sync to surface risks for current Private rollouts, unblock Dedicated->Private parity items, and align on canary plan for next two customer installs. Tone: tactical, short decisions, explicit owners.

Agenda (15m):
- Rollout status and recent incidents (5m)
- Canary plan & test matrix (4m)
- Security / compliance open items (3m)
- Action items & blockers (3m)

Rollout status:
- Two customers in Private trial: BlueBank (EU VPC) and MediSoft (US on-prem EKS). BlueBank: install completed but post-install validation 85% pass (target 95%). Failure modes predominantly around network egress policy and KMS key policy mapping.
- MediSoft: initial package deployment succeeded; observed degraded inference latency on RTX A5000 nodes under burst load (p95 ~ 420ms, expected <300ms). SRE investigating kernel tuning + batching defaults.
- Canary pass rate across last 3 installs: 78% (down from 88% last month) — need root cause before expanding.

Incidents and notes:
- INC-4321: customer reported audit log gaps for admin actions when HSM key rotation was simulated. Tomoko has reproducer; currently root cause: race condition between rotation webhook and audit flush.
- On-call blip: autoscaler flapped during MediSoft throughput ramp; suspected kube-controller-manager bump introduced jitter. Kara pointed at controller logs; Marco will correlate with autoscaler metrics.

Canary plan (next 2 weeks):
- Objective: validate KMS rotation flow + autoscaler stability across two hardware profiles (A5000, H100-80GB emulated).
- Test matrix:
  * KMS rotation simulated under 0/50/500 concurrent requests; check audit logs, reconnect behavior, and request latencies.
  * Autoscaler ramp tests: step up to sustained 250 qps for 10m then ramp down; observe Pod churn, queue latency, and p95 token latency.
  * Quantization toggle: run v1 (int8) vs v2 (int4) model bundles to ensure fallback and warning telemetry works.
- Owners: Marco owns autoscaler tests (due 2026-05-28), Linnea owns canary acceptance criteria doc (due 2026-05-25), Ravi coordinates customer-facing schedule (reach out to BlueBank/MediSoft ops today).

Security & compliance items:
- HSM/KMS mapping: outstanding mapping doc for cross-account key policies. Action: Tomoko to deliver policy snippets + review checklist by 2026-05-26.
- Audit retention: product asked for 90-day vs current 30-day retention as opt-in. Need impact analysis on storage costs (Bryan in Finance to be looped). Status: draft sent to Product.
- Air-gapped packaging: small packaging issue found where telemetry stub was unintentionally pulled in. Decision: make telemetry optional at package build time; action Tomoko + EngInfra to add build flag (JIRA-PD-712).

Decisions made in this meeting:
- Freeze expanding canary pool until autoscaler and KMS rotation passes are green. (Decision owner: Aisha)
- Make telemetry opt-out explicit for air-gapped bundles; unblock MediSoft install immediately with opt-out. (Owner: Tomoko, due 2026-05-24)

Open blockers:
- Kernel tuning guidance for A5000 under burst inference — SRE needs to validate sysctl changes and coordinate with Release Engineering for a hotfix image. (Owner: Marco, blocker until validated)
- Discrepancy between audit events emitted by runtime and control plane during rotation — high priority for compliance customers. (Owner: Tomoko)
- Test infra instability: one of the canary runners failed with intermittent disk pressure; CICD infra ticket created (PD-INFRA-89).

Action items (explicit):
- Marco: run autoscaler ramp matrix and produce telemetry dashboard chart + PR to runbook for threshold tuning. Due 2026-05-28.
- Linnea: finalize canary acceptance criteria doc, include pass/fail thresholds and rollback triggers; link to Confluence. Due 2026-05-25.
- Tomoko: deliver KMS policy snippets, telemetry opt-out build flag, and reproducer for audit race. Due 2026-05-26 (audit reproducer) and 2026-05-24 (telemetry flag).
- Ravi: confirm customer maintenance windows for two canary installs and send calendar invites; note any ops constraints. Due EOD 2026-05-22.
- Kara: correlate on-call logs with autoscaler events and add timeline to INC-4321. Due 2026-05-23.

Metrics snapshot (quick):
- Canary install success: 78% (target 95%)
- Average install time: 42m (goal <30m)
- p95 inference latency (A5000): 420ms observed during burst; expected <300ms
- Audit event delivery success: 98% for normal ops, drops to ~70% during KMS rotation simulation

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: rolling out before fixing audit gap could fail customer SOC2 audits. Mitigation: block rollouts for customers requiring >30-day retention or immediate audit fidelity; offer isolated trial with manual verification.
- Risk: aggressive autoscaler thresholds cause oscillation in first-week traffic for some customers. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds + telemetry-derived adaptive tuning (follow-up runway 3 weeks).

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Consider a short "private-deployments hardening sprint" (2 weeks) to clear top 5 install regressions; pick top owners and freeze new feature merges.
- Need a shared runbook for KMS rotation that spans runtime, control plane, and audit pipeline — current docs live in three places. Consolidate into single Confluence page and link from install checklist.

Next meeting: quick sync (15m) Tuesday 2026-05-26 to review canary acceptance doc and autoscaler test results.

Unresolved questions:
- If we apply sysctl tuning for A5000, what is the supported matrix going forward? (release engineering input required)
- Do we need to change SLA language for private installs while these regressions are open? (legal/product)

Quick links / references:
- Canary criteria draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/canary-criteria-draft
- Reproducer for rotation race: github.com/redwood-inference/rot-repro (Tomoko owns)
- Inc ticket: JIRA-INC-4321

End of notes.

Patch-style edits welcome — doc is intentionally minimal and tactical.
